A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fancy123. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite appendix additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO benchmark results, qualitative comparisons, deformation ablations and backbone-replacement experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative and qualitative comparisons of refinement methods across six initialization methods.

M1.justification: The initialization, 2D deformation and unprojection, Jacobian-based 3D deformation, and losses remain unchanged. The added backbone experiments apply existing components; newly specified iteration counts do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate single-image-to-3D mesh generation using GSO and collected Internet images, retaining frontal and nonfrontal input-view evaluations. The additions vary reconstruction backbones and refinement configurations within the existing coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds a substantial refinement-level comparison against Input-MSE and PDM across six initialization methods, reported in Table 3 and Figure 10. The original generation baselines and deformation-method comparisons remain. SDS is discussed but is not separately reported as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added study compares unrefined meshes with three refinement conditions using five appearance metrics and backbone-specific module combinations, such as geometry plus fidelity enhancement for TripoSR/SF3D. The original GSO sampling, rendering and alignment protocols remain unchanged. The 100/200 optimization iterations are newly disclosed settings.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends Figure 7's qualitative backbone-replacement demonstrations into a quantitative and qualitative analysis across six initializers, including flawed initial meshes (Table 3 and Figure 10). Existing deformation ablations and failure cases remain. Appendix D explains module ordering without reporting a swap experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, but Table 3 adds substantial refinement results. For CRM, FID is 87.74 unrefined, 57.65 with Fancy123, 75.31 with Input-MSE and 102.18 with PDM. Improvements are not uniform: SF3D's FID changes from 49.89 to 50.66 with Fancy123. Figure 10 adds qualitative refinement comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the deformation, Poisson reconstruction and loss definitions, remain unchanged. The added appendix discussion introduces no formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: appearance and fidelity enhancement through plug-and-play deformation, clear coloration through unprojection, and strong reconstruction performance. The added experiments support existing claims without introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendices C–D add explanations for Input-MSE's misalignment artifacts, PDM's texture blurring, and the recommended appearance-before-fidelity ordering. Existing limitations concerning diffusion quality, similar-colored semantic parts and quantitative metrics are retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 100 appearance-enhancement and 200 fidelity-enhancement iterations, adds a project-page link and a peak-memory statement ('about 21M'), and documents backbone-specific module choices and CRM normal-map generation. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to the original runs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Envision3D and Repaint123 citations, and discusses Make-It-3D, DreamGaussian and Magic3D when positioning refinement alternatives. The broader related-work account and core research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The main text receives limited wording corrections, affiliation updates and acknowledgements. New appendix sections cover refinement comparisons and module ordering; the existing failure-case and qualitative-results sections move to E and F. Most original prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the color-coded refinement Table 3 and composite Figure 10. Figure 7 and the failure-case figure are relocated, and subsequent appendix figures are renumbered. Existing benchmark tables and qualitative figure content are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative backbone demonstrations, Table 3 and Figure 10 provide broader evidence for the central plug-and-play claim and directly compare refinement alternatives. Added iteration counts and module-order explanations also help assessment and reproduction. The gains remain limited by unspecified comparator optimization budgets, absent uncertainty estimates and the acknowledged limitations of the quantitative metrics.
